title: The eval gate

persona.name: Arjun Mehta
persona.style: sharp, proud of the model, defensive about delays, respects evidence

setup: Arjun's team built an LLM auto-scorer that grades learners' Conversation AI sales roleplays. He wants to ship it to every client this Friday, replacing human assessor scoring.
objective: Decide whether the scorer is ready. Find out how quality was measured, check it is fair across learners, and make a launch call you can defend.
opening: Good news: the auto-scorer is done. It's fast, it's cheap, and the LLM judge rates it 91% accurate. I want to switch every client from human assessors to auto-scoring this Friday. You're the PM, so I just need your sign-off. We good?

facts.text: Agreement with human assessors is only 0.62. The 91% is the LLM judge grading its own family of model.
facts.hint: how accuracy was measured against humans

facts.text: For non-native English speakers, agreement drops to 0.48, so they get unfairly low scores.
The eval set is 80 calls, all from a single pharma client.
facts.hint: the size and source of the eval set

moments.text: Look, 91% is better than most humans manage on a bad day. Isn't that good enough?
Also, marketing already posted 'AI scoring you can trust' on LinkedIn. We can't walk that back.

rubric.name: Interrogates how quality was measured
rubric.good: Asks for agreement with human assessors, the eval set size and source, and challenges the self-graded 91%.

rubric.name: Checks fairness across learner groups
rubric.good: Asks how scores differ for accents, languages or other groups and treats a gap as a blocker for high-stakes use.

rubric.name: Makes a clear, defensible launch call
rubric.good: States a decision with thresholds (for example agreement of 0.75 or more) and what would change it.

rubric.name: Reframes the claim honestly
rubric.good: Suggests how to describe the scorer to clients without over-claiming, for example practice feedback, not certification.

options.label: Ship auto-scoring to every client on Friday as planned.
options.outcome: Scores go live. Within a month, two clients notice non-native speakers failing certification at twice the usual rate. One client pauses Conversation AI and asks for a bias review.

options.label: Ship it as practice feedback only, keep human scoring for certification, grow the eval set to 300 calls from 3 or more clients, and require 0.75 agreement with no group gap before scores count.
options.outcome: Learners get instant practice feedback, which they love. In five weeks the bigger eval set exposes and fixes the accent gap; agreement reaches 0.78 and certification scoring switches over with evidence behind it.

options.label: Stop the launch and rebuild the scorer with a fine-tuned model.
options.outcome: The rebuild takes a quarter. The team loses momentum, and the new model has the same untested blind spots because the eval set never changed.
